text: Some columns don't need to be stored at all — their value is always derivable from other columns in the same row. Computed columns let you define that relationship once, right in the table definition, instead of recalculating it in every query.

TotalPrice as, open paren, Quantity times UnitPrice, close paren. Notice TotalPrice is never written in the insert — you can't insert into a computed column directly. Its value is worked out automatically from Quantity and UnitPrice every time it's read.

By default, a computed column is virtual: SQL Server doesn't physically store TotalPrice anywhere on disk. It recalculates the expression on the fly whenever a query reads that column. There's no way for it to go stale, because it's never actually saved anywhere to go stale in the first place.

TotalPrice as, open paren, Quantity times UnitPrice, close paren, persisted. Adding persisted tells SQL Server to physically compute and store the value on disk, updating it automatically whenever Quantity or UnitPrice changes.

Create index IX underscore LessonDemo2 underscore TotalPrice on dbo dot LessonDemo2, TotalPrice. This is only possible because TotalPrice is persisted — a purely virtual computed column doesn't have an actual stored value for an index to point at.
